subject: physics

items.q: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, how do pressure and volume relate?
items.correct: Inversely — halve the volume and the pressure doubles (p₁V₁ = p₂V₂).
items.misconception: Directly — increase the volume and the pressure increases too.
items.why: Boyle's law: squeezing a gas into a smaller volume makes particles strike the walls more often, raising the pressure.

items.q: What does specific heat capacity tell you?
items.correct: The energy needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C.
items.misconception: The temperature at which a substance melts.
items.random_wrong: How hot a substance can get before it boils.
items.why: Specific heat capacity (Q = mcΔθ) is about energy stored per degree of temperature rise — not a fixed temperature.

items.q: Why does water need lots of energy to boil even once it reaches 100°C?
items.correct: Latent heat is needed to separate the particles into a gas, with no temperature change.
items.misconception: Once at 100°C it boils instantly with no extra energy.
items.random_wrong: Boiling actually cools the water down.
items.why: Specific latent heat of vaporisation (Q = mL) is the energy needed to turn liquid into gas at constant temperature.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics (4PH1) specification; Solids, Liquids & Gases
